epithet.en: Ambitious scientist, creator of the Creature

4.modern-en: Walton rescues a half-frozen stranger from the ice. The man is wasted and feverish but agrees to board when he learns the ship is heading north. Walton nurses him and is captivated by his intelligence and sorrow.
4.modern-da: Walton redder en halvt frosset fremmed fra isen. Manden er udmattet og febrilsk, men går om bord, da han hører, skibet sejler nordpå. Walton plejer ham og fængsles af hans intelligens og sorg.

5.modern-en: Begins narrating his life story. Describes his happy childhood in Geneva, his parents' devotion, and his early fascination with the works of Cornelius Agrippa and other alchemists.
5.modern-da: Begynder at fortælle sin livshistorie. Beskriver sin lykkelige barndom i Genève, forældrenes kærlighed og sin tidlige fascination af Cornelius Agrippa og andre alkymister.

6.modern-en: Recounts his growing obsession with natural philosophy and the secret of life. A lightning strike destroys a tree and sparks his interest in electricity and galvanism.
6.modern-da: Fortæller om sin voksende besættelse af naturfilosofi og livets hemmelighed. Et lynnedslag ødelægger et træ og vækker hans interesse for elektricitet og galvanisme.

7.modern-en: Arrives at the University of Ingolstadt after his mother's death. Professors Krempe and Waldman inspire him to pursue modern chemistry and anatomy. He throws himself into study with feverish intensity.
7.modern-da: Ankommer til universitetet i Ingolstadt efter sin mors død. Professorerne Krempe og Waldman inspirerer ham til at forfølge moderne kemi og anatomi. Han kaster sig over studierne med febrilsk intensitet.

8.modern-en: After two years of obsessive work collecting body parts from charnel houses and dissecting rooms, he nears completion of his creation. His health deteriorates and he isolates himself from family and friends.
8.modern-da: Efter to års besættende arbejde med at samle kropsdele fra lighuse og dissektionsstuer nærmer han sig færdiggørelsen af sin skabning. Hans helbred forværres, og han isolerer sig fra familie og venner.

9.modern-en: Brings the Creature to life on a dreary November night, then recoils in horror at its appearance. Flees his apartment and wanders the streets in a frenzy. Clerval arrives and Victor collapses into months of nervous fever.
9.modern-da: Giver Væsenet liv en trist novembernat, men viger tilbage i rædsel over dets udseende. Flygter fra sin lejlighed og vandrer febrilsk rundt i gaderne. Clerval ankommer, og Victor bryder sammen i måneders nervefeber.

10.modern-en: Recovers slowly under Clerval's care. Receives a letter from Elizabeth. Dreads any mention of natural philosophy. Takes up Oriental languages with Clerval as a distraction from his guilt.
10.modern-da: Kommer sig langsomt under Clervals pleje. Modtager et brev fra Elizabeth. Gyser ved enhver omtale af naturfilosofi. Begynder at studere østerlandske sprog med Clerval som afledning fra sin skyld.

11.modern-en: Receives his father's letter announcing William's murder. Rushes toward Geneva. During a storm near the city, he glimpses the Creature and becomes instantly certain it killed William.
11.modern-da: Modtager sin fars brev om Williams mord. Skynder sig mod Genève. Under en storm nær byen skimter han Væsenet og bliver øjeblikkeligt overbevist om, at det dræbte William.

12.modern-en: Attends Justine's trial, convinced of her innocence but unable to reveal the true murderer without being thought insane. Suffers in agonized silence as she is condemned and executed.
12.modern-da: Overværer Justines retssag, overbevist om hendes uskyld, men ude af stand til at afsløre den sande morder uden at blive anset for sindssyg. Lider i pinefuld tavshed, mens hun dømmes og henrettes.

13.modern-en: Overwhelmed by guilt over William's and Justine's deaths. Retreats into isolation and dark melancholy. Takes solitary boat trips on the lake and wanders the Alps seeking relief.
13.modern-da: Overvældet af skyld over Williams og Justines død. Trækker sig tilbage i isolation og dyster melankoli. Tager ensomme bådture på søen og vandrer i Alperne for at finde lindring.

14.modern-en: Travels to Chamonix seeking peace in nature. Encounters the Creature on the Mer de Glace glacier. The Creature demands a hearing, and Victor reluctantly agrees to listen.
14.modern-da: Rejser til Chamonix for at søge fred i naturen. Møder Væsenet på Mer de Glace-gletsjeren. Væsenet kræver at blive hørt, og Victor accepterer modvilligt at lytte.

19.modern-en: Mentioned by the Creature: Victor's journal, found in the coat pocket, reveals the full details of the creation, filling the Creature with anguish and rage at his maker.
19.modern-da: Nævnt af Væsenet: Victors dagbog, fundet i frakkelommen, afslører alle skabelsens detaljer og fylder Væsenet med pine og raseri mod sin skaber.

21.modern-en: Listens as the Creature demands a female companion. Initially refuses, then is moved by the Creature's arguments and promises. Reluctantly agrees, on the condition the pair will leave humanity forever.
21.modern-da: Lytter, mens Væsenet kræver en kvindelig ledsager. Nægter først, men bevæges af Væsenets argumenter og løfter. Accepterer modvilligt på betingelse af, at parret forlader menneskeheden for evigt.

22.modern-en: Unable to begin the loathsome work, he stalls for months. His father proposes marriage to Elizabeth. Victor arranges a trip to England to gather scientific knowledge needed for the second creation.
22.modern-da: Ude af stand til at begynde det modbydelige arbejde udsætter han det i måneder. Hans far foreslår ægteskab med Elizabeth. Victor arrangerer en rejse til England for at samle den nødvendige videnskabelige viden.

23.modern-en: Travels through England and Scotland with Clerval. Parts from his friend at Perth and retreats to a remote Orkney island to build the female creature in solitude.
23.modern-da: Rejser gennem England og Skotland med Clerval. Tager afsked med sin ven i Perth og trækker sig tilbage til en fjern ørkenø ved Orkney for at bygge det kvindelige væsen i ensomhed.

24.modern-en: Sees the Creature watching through his window and, seized by horror at the consequences, tears the half-finished female to pieces. The Creature threatens revenge: 'I shall be with you on your wedding night.'
24.modern-da: Ser Væsenet kigge ind gennem vinduet og river i rædsel over konsekvenserne den halvfærdige kvinde i stykker. Væsenet truer med hævn: 'Jeg skal være hos dig på din bryllupsnat.'

25.modern-en: Brought before an Irish magistrate, suspected of murder. Sees Clerval's strangled body and collapses in agonized convulsions. Falls into months of feverish delirium in prison. His father arrives and he is eventually acquitted.
25.modern-da: Stilles for en irsk dommer, mistænkt for mord. Ser Clervals kvalte lig og bryder sammen i smertefulde kramper. Falder i måneders febrilsk delirium i fængslet. Hans far ankommer, og han frikendes til sidst.

26.modern-en: Returns to Geneva shattered. Receives Elizabeth's letter asking if he truly loves her. Interprets the Creature's threat as meaning his own death on the wedding night. Agrees to the marriage, keeping his secret.
26.modern-da: Vender knust tilbage til Genève. Modtager Elizabeths brev, der spørger, om han virkelig elsker hende. Tolker Væsenets trussel som sin egen død på bryllupsnatten. Indvilliger i ægteskabet og bevarer sin hemmelighed.

27.modern-en: Marries Elizabeth and they travel to Evian. While Victor searches the inn for the Creature, Elizabeth is strangled in the bridal chamber. He fires at the fleeing monster but misses. Elizabeth is dead.
27.modern-da: Gifter sig med Elizabeth, og de rejser til Evian. Mens Victor gennemsøger kroen for Væsenet, kvæles Elizabeth i brudekammeret. Han skyder efter det flygtende monster, men rammer ikke. Elizabeth er død.

28.modern-en: His father dies of grief. Victor is briefly confined to an asylum. Vows vengeance and pursues the Creature across Europe, Russia, and into the Arctic. Rescued by Walton's ship, he tells his story and dies aboard, urging Walton to destroy the Creature.
28.modern-da: Hans far dør af sorg. Victor indsættes kortvarigt på en anstalt. Sværger hævn og forfølger Væsenet gennem Europa, Rusland og ind i Arktis. Reddes af Waltons skib, fortæller sin historie og dør om bord med en bøn om, at Walton tilintetgør Væsenet.

epithet.en: Frankenstein's abandoned creation, seeking love and vengeance
epithet.da: Frankensteins forladte skabning, der søger kærlighed og hævn

4.modern-en: Seen from the ship as a gigantic figure driving a dog sledge across the Arctic ice the night before Walton rescues Victor. He is the quarry Victor has been pursuing.
4.modern-da: Ses fra skibet som en kæmpemæssig skikkelse, der kører en hundeslæde over den arktiske is natten før Walton redder Victor. Han er byttet, Victor har forfulgt.

9.modern-en: Brought to life on a dreary November night. Opens his dull yellow eye. Reaches toward Victor, who flees in horror. Disappears from the apartment before morning.
9.modern-da: Vækkes til live en trist novembernat. Åbner sit matte gule øje. Rækker ud mod Victor, der flygter i rædsel. Forsvinder fra lejligheden inden morgenen.

11.modern-en: Glimpsed by Victor during a thunderstorm near Geneva, scaling Mount Salève with superhuman speed. Victor instantly concludes the Creature murdered William.
11.modern-da: Skimtes af Victor under en tordenstorm nær Genève, mens han klatrer op ad Mont Salève med overmenneskelig hast. Victor konkluderer øjeblikkeligt, at Væsenet myrdede William.

14.modern-en: Confronts Victor on the Mer de Glace glacier and demands to be heard. Eloquently argues that his creator owes him justice. Victor reluctantly agrees to listen to his story.
14.modern-da: Konfronterer Victor på Mer de Glace-gletsjeren og kræver at blive hørt. Argumenterer veltalende for, at hans skaber skylder ham retfærdighed. Victor accepterer modvilligt at lytte til hans historie.

15.modern-en: Narrates his earliest days: confused sensations of light, hunger, and cold. Wanders alone through forests, learning to distinguish his senses. Discovers fire and takes shelter near the De Lacey cottage.
15.modern-da: Fortæller om sine tidligste dage: forvirrede sanseindtryk af lys, sult og kulde. Vandrer alene gennem skove og lærer at skelne sine sanser. Opdager ild og søger ly nær De Lacey-hytten.

16.modern-en: Observes the De Lacey family from his hiding place. Learns their language by watching and listening. Begins to understand human society, family bonds, and his own terrible isolation.
16.modern-da: Observerer De Lacey-familien fra sit skjulested. Lærer deres sprog ved at se og lytte. Begynder at forstå menneskeligt samfund, familiebånd og sin egen frygtelige isolation.

17.modern-en: Watches Safie arrive and observes the family's joy. Learns to read alongside her using Volney's Ruins of Empires. Grasps human history and society but agonizes over his own hideous appearance and utter solitude.
17.modern-da: Ser Safie ankomme og observerer familiens glæde. Lærer at læse sammen med hende via Volneys Ruins of Empires. Forstår menneskets historie og samfund, men pines over sit eget afskyelige udseende og totale ensomhed.

18.modern-en: Learns the De Lacey family's backstory: their fall from wealth in Paris, Felix's rescue of Safie's father, and their unjust exile. Deepens his empathy and longing for acceptance.
18.modern-da: Lærer De Lacey-familiens baggrundshistorie: deres fald fra rigdom i Paris, Felix' redning af Safies far og deres uretfærdige eksil. Hans empati og længsel efter accept uddybes.

19.modern-en: Reads Paradise Lost, Plutarch's Lives, and The Sorrows of Young Werther — identifying with both Adam and Satan. Discovers Victor's journal and learns the truth of his creation. Resolves to approach the cottagers: enters when De Lacey is alone and wins the blind man's sympathy, but Felix returns and beats him violently. Flees in anguish, his hopes of acceptance destroyed.
19.modern-da: Læser Det tabte Paradis, Plutarchs Levnedsbeskrivelser og Den unge Werthers lidelser — identificerer sig med både Adam og Satan. Opdager Victors dagbog og lærer sandheden om sin skabelse. Beslutter sig for at nærme sig familien: træder ind, mens De Lacey er alene, og vinder den blinde mands medfølelse, men Felix vender tilbage og slår ham voldsomt. Flygter i pine, og hans håb om accept er knust.

20.modern-en: Returns to find the De Laceys have fled. Burns the cottage in rage. Journeys toward Geneva to confront his creator. Saves a drowning girl but is shot by her companion. Near Geneva, encounters young William and strangles him. Plants the portrait on the sleeping Justine. Demands Victor create a female companion.
20.modern-da: Vender tilbage og finder, at De Lacey-familien er flygtet. Brænder hytten i raseri. Rejser mod Genève for at konfrontere sin skaber. Redder en druknende pige, men skydes af hendes ledsager. Nær Genève møder han den lille William og kvæler ham. Placerer portrættet på den sovende Justine. Kræver, at Victor skaber en kvindelig ledsager.

21.modern-en: Pleads for a female companion with eloquence and pathos. Promises to leave humanity forever if Victor agrees. Victor, moved by his arguments and fearful of his power, reluctantly consents.
21.modern-da: Bønfalder med veltalenhed og patos om en kvindelig ledsager. Lover at forlade menneskeheden for evigt, hvis Victor accepterer. Victor, bevæget af hans argumenter og bange for hans magt, indvilliger modvilligt.

24.modern-en: Watches through the window as Victor destroys the half-finished female. Confronts Victor in a rage, delivering the chilling threat: 'I shall be with you on your wedding night.' Departs by boat into the darkness.
24.modern-da: Kigger ind gennem vinduet, mens Victor ødelægger den halvfærdige kvinde. Konfronterer Victor i raseri og fremsætter den iskolde trussel: 'Jeg skal være hos dig på din bryllupsnat.' Forsvinder med båd ud i mørket.

25.modern-en: Murders Henry Clerval by strangulation in Ireland, leaving the body where Victor will be blamed. This is his vengeance for the destruction of the female creature.
25.modern-da: Myrder Henry Clerval ved kvælning i Irland og efterlader liget, så Victor får skylden. Dette er hans hævn for ødelæggelsen af det kvindelige væsen.

27.modern-en: Strangles Elizabeth on her wedding night at the inn in Evian. Grins through the window at Victor as he points at the corpse, then escapes into the lake.
27.modern-da: Kvæler Elizabeth på hendes bryllupsnat på kroen i Evian. Griner gennem vinduet til Victor, mens han peger på liget, og flygter derefter ud i søen.

28.modern-en: Leads Victor on a chase across Europe and into the Arctic, leaving taunting messages. After Victor dies aboard Walton's ship, the Creature appears over his body, weeping with remorse. Declares he will burn himself on a funeral pyre at the North Pole and vanishes into the darkness.
28.modern-da: Leder Victor på en jagt gennem Europa og ind i Arktis og efterlader hånende beskeder. Efter Victors død om bord på Waltons skib dukker Væsenet op over hans lig og græder af anger. Erklærer, at han vil brænde sig selv på et bål ved Nordpolen og forsvinder ud i mørket.

1.modern-en: Writes to his sister Margaret from St. Petersburg, describing his lifelong dream of reaching the North Pole. Recounts his youthful ambitions, self-education, and preparations for the expedition.
1.modern-da: Skriver til sin søster Margaret fra Sankt Petersborg og beskriver sin livslange drøm om at nå Nordpolen. Fortæller om sine ungdommelige ambitioner, selvuddannelse og forberedelser til ekspeditionen.

2.modern-en: Writes from Archangel about hiring his ship and crew. Laments his lack of a true friend who could share his joys and temper his ambitions. Describes his kind-hearted ship's master.
2.modern-da: Skriver fra Arkhangelsk om at have hyret sit skib og sin besætning. Beklager manglen på en sand ven, der kan dele hans glæder og dæmpe hans ambitioner. Beskriver sin godhjertede skibsfører.

3.modern-en: Writes briefly to confirm he is making good progress northward. His spirits are high and his crew is resolute. Expresses confidence in the expedition's success.
3.modern-da: Skriver kort for at bekræfte, at han gør gode fremskridt nordpå. Hans humør er højt, og besætningen er beslutsom. Udtrykker tillid til ekspeditionens succes.

4.modern-en: Records seeing a gigantic figure on a dog sledge across the ice. The next morning rescues a half-frozen European man (Victor) from a drifting ice raft. Nurses him and begins to form a deep attachment.
4.modern-da: Beskriver synet af en kæmpemæssig skikkelse på en hundeslæde over isen. Næste morgen redder han en halvt frosset europæisk mand (Victor) fra en drivende isflage. Plejer ham og begynder at knytte sig dybt til ham.

28.modern-en: Records Victor's final days and death aboard the ship. Faces mutiny from his crew and agrees to turn south. Encounters the Creature mourning over Victor's body. The Creature declares his intention to die and vanishes onto the ice.
28.modern-da: Beretter om Victors sidste dage og død om bord på skibet. Står over for mytteri fra sin besætning og accepterer at vende sydpå. Møder Væsenet, der sørger over Victors lig. Væsenet erklærer sin hensigt om at dø og forsvinder ud på isen.

5.modern-en: Described as an orphan adopted into the Frankenstein household. Bright, gentle, and beloved by the entire family. She and Victor grow up as the closest companions.
5.modern-da: Beskrives som en forældreløs, der er adopteret ind i familien Frankenstein. Klog, blid og elsket af hele familien. Hun og Victor vokser op som de nærmeste ledsagere.

10.modern-en: Writes a long letter to Victor during his recovery, updating him on family life, Justine Moritz's return, and little William's growth. Her warmth and devotion shine through every line.
10.modern-da: Skriver et langt brev til Victor under hans rekonvalescens med nyt om familielivet, Justine Moritz' tilbagevenden og lille Williams opvækst. Hendes varme og hengivenhed lyser igennem hver linje.

11.modern-en: Mentioned in Alphonse's letter as grief-stricken over William's murder, blaming herself because the portrait miniature she lent him drew the killer.
11.modern-da: Nævnes i Alphonses brev som knust af sorg over Williams mord og bebrejder sig selv, fordi portrætminiaturen, hun lånte ham, tiltrak morderen.

12.modern-en: Defends Justine passionately at the trial, testifying to her good character. Her eloquent appeal moves the courtroom but fails to save Justine. Visits Justine in prison with Victor.
12.modern-da: Forsvarer Justine lidenskabeligt under retssagen og vidner om hendes gode karakter. Hendes veltalende appel bevæger retssalen, men redder ikke Justine. Besøger Justine i fængslet sammen med Victor.

13.modern-en: Mentioned as deeply affected by William's and Justine's deaths. Her grief mirrors Victor's, though hers is the misery of innocence rather than guilt.
13.modern-da: Nævnes som dybt påvirket af Williams og Justines død. Hendes sorg afspejler Victors, men hendes er uskyldige menneskers lidelse, ikke skyldens.

26.modern-en: Writes to Victor asking whether he truly loves her or feels bound only by duty. Her letter is gentle and selfless, wanting only his happiness. Victor, interpreting the Creature's threat as his own death, agrees to the marriage.
26.modern-da: Skriver til Victor og spørger, om han virkelig elsker hende, eller om han kun føler sig bundet af pligt. Hendes brev er mildt og uselvisk, og hun ønsker kun hans lykke. Victor, der tolker Væsenets trussel som sin egen død, indvilliger i ægteskabet.

27.modern-en: Marries Victor and they travel by boat to Evian. She is melancholy despite the beautiful day, sensing something terrible. Retires to the bridal chamber where the Creature strangles her. Victor finds her body thrown across the bed.
27.modern-da: Gifter sig med Victor, og de rejser med båd til Evian. Hun er melankolsk trods den smukke dag og aner noget frygteligt. Trækker sig tilbage til brudekammeret, hvor Væsenet kvæler hende. Victor finder hendes lig kastet hen over sengen.

epithet.en: Victor's loyal and joyful best friend
epithet.da: Victors loyale og livsglade bedste ven

5.modern-en: Described as Victor's childhood friend, imaginative and full of enterprise. His father initially resists sending him to university, wanting him in business.
5.modern-da: Beskrives som Victors barndomsven, fantasifuld og fuld af virkelyst. Hans far modsætter sig først at sende ham på universitetet og vil have ham i forretningslivet.

9.modern-en: Arrives at Ingolstadt just as Victor brings the Creature to life. Finds his friend in a state of wild, incoherent agitation. Nurses Victor through months of nervous fever, keeping the illness secret from the family.
9.modern-da: Ankommer til Ingolstadt, netop som Victor vækker Væsenet til live. Finder sin ven i en tilstand af vild, usammenhængende uro. Plejer Victor gennem måneders nervefeber og holder sygdommen skjult for familien.

10.modern-en: Introduces Victor to Oriental languages as a therapeutic distraction. His gentle companionship and enthusiasm for life slowly restore Victor's spirits and love of nature.
10.modern-da: Introducerer Victor for østerlandske sprog som terapeutisk afledning. Hans milde selskab og livsentusiasme genopretter langsomt Victors livsmod og kærlighed til naturen.

11.modern-en: Reads Alphonse's letter about William's death with Victor. Tries to console his friend. Arranges the horses for Victor's immediate departure to Geneva.
11.modern-da: Læser Alphonses brev om Williams død sammen med Victor. Forsøger at trøste sin ven. Arrangerer hestene til Victors øjeblikkelige afrejse til Genève.

22.modern-en: Joins Victor on the journey to England, arranged by Victor's father. His joyful observations of the Rhine landscape and English countryside contrast sharply with Victor's inner torment.
22.modern-da: Slutter sig til Victor på rejsen til England, arrangeret af Victors far. Hans glade observationer af Rhinlandskabet og det engelske landskab står i skarp kontrast til Victors indre pine.

23.modern-en: Thrives in London and Scotland, making contacts for his planned venture to India. Reluctantly parts from Victor at Perth when Victor insists on traveling alone to the Orkneys.
23.modern-da: Trives i London og Skotland og knytter kontakter til sit planlagte indienprojekt. Tager modvilligt afsked med Victor i Perth, da Victor insisterer på at rejse alene til Orkney.

25.modern-en: Found murdered by strangulation on an Irish shore — the Creature's victim. Victor, brought before the body, collapses in convulsions upon recognizing his dearest friend.
25.modern-da: Fundet myrdet ved kvælning på en irsk kyst — Væsenets offer. Victor, der stilles over for liget, bryder sammen i kramper, da han genkender sin kæreste ven.

5.modern-en: Described as a respected Genevese public official who married Caroline Beaufort after rescuing her from poverty following her father's death. A devoted and loving parent.
5.modern-da: Beskrives som en respekteret genèvisk embedsmand, der giftede sig med Caroline Beaufort efter at have reddet hende fra fattigdom efter hendes fars død. En hengiven og kærlig far.

8.modern-en: Writes occasional letters to Victor at university but never reproaches him for his silence, only gently asking about his work.
8.modern-da: Skriver lejlighedsvise breve til Victor på universitetet, men bebrejder ham aldrig hans tavshed og spørger blot mildt til hans arbejde.

11.modern-en: Writes the devastating letter informing Victor of William's murder. Urges Victor to come home with feelings of peace rather than vengeance.
11.modern-da: Skriver det ødelæggende brev, der informerer Victor om Williams mord. Opfordrer Victor til at komme hjem med følelser af fred snarere end hævn.

12.modern-en: Attends Justine's trial with the family. Believes in her innocence and trusts the justice system, urging Elizabeth not to lose hope.
12.modern-da: Overværer Justines retssag sammen med familien. Tror på hendes uskyld og stoler på retssystemet, og opfordrer Elizabeth til ikke at miste håbet.

22.modern-en: Notices Victor's lingering depression and gently broaches the subject of marriage to Elizabeth, hoping it will restore his son's happiness. Arranges for Clerval to accompany Victor to England.
22.modern-da: Bemærker Victors vedvarende depression og bringer forsigtigt ægteskabet med Elizabeth på bane i håb om at genoprette sin søns lykke. Arrangerer, at Clerval ledsager Victor til England.

25.modern-en: Travels to Ireland after receiving Kirwin's letter about Victor's arrest. His arrival brings Victor comfort during his imprisonment. Overjoyed when the charges are dismissed.
25.modern-da: Rejser til Irland efter at have modtaget Kirwins brev om Victors arrestation. Hans ankomst bringer Victor trøst under hans fængsel. Overvældet af glæde, da anklagerne frafaldes.

26.modern-en: Urges Victor to marry Elizabeth soon, hoping it will cure his melancholy. His advanced age and deep concern for his son's well-being make every delay painful to him.
26.modern-da: Opfordrer Victor til at gifte sig med Elizabeth snart i håb om at helbrede hans melankoli. Hans fremskredne alder og dybe bekymring for sin søns velbefindende gør enhver forsinkelse smertefuld.

27.modern-en: Mentioned as overjoyed at the wedding. He is at home in Geneva while Victor and Elizabeth travel to Evian.
27.modern-da: Nævnes som overlykkelig over brylluppet. Han er hjemme i Genève, mens Victor og Elizabeth rejser til Evian.

28.modern-en: Collapses upon hearing of Elizabeth's murder. The accumulated grief — William, Justine, Clerval, and now Elizabeth — is too much. He dies within days, broken by sorrow.
28.modern-da: Bryder sammen ved nyheden om Elizabeths mord. Den ophobede sorg — William, Justine, Clerval og nu Elizabeth — er for meget. Han dør inden for få dage, knækket af sorg.

epithet.en: Victor's youngest brother, the Creature's first victim
epithet.da: Victors yngste bror, Væsenets første offer

10.modern-en: Described lovingly in Elizabeth's letter as a sweet, laughing boy with blue eyes and curly hair, adored by the whole family.
10.modern-da: Beskrives kærligt i Elizabeths brev som en sød, leende dreng med blå øjne og krøllet hår, tilbedt af hele familien.

11.modern-en: Found murdered in the fields of Plainpalais with the marks of fingers on his neck. His death — and the missing portrait miniature — set the tragedy in motion.
11.modern-da: Fundet myrdet på Plainpalais' marker med fingeraftryk på halsen. Hans død — og det forsvundne portrætminiature — sætter tragedien i gang.

20.modern-en: The Creature recounts killing William: he encountered the boy near Geneva, hoped to make him a companion, but strangled him in rage when the child revealed he was a Frankenstein.
20.modern-da: Væsenet fortæller om drabet på William: han mødte drengen nær Genève, håbede at gøre ham til ledsager, men kvalte ham i raseri, da barnet afslørede, at han var en Frankenstein.

epithet.en: Faithful family servant, wrongly executed for William's murder
epithet.da: Trofast familietjener, uretmæssigt henrettet for Williams mord

10.modern-en: Elizabeth describes her history: adopted into the Frankenstein household, devoted to Madame Frankenstein, she nursed both her protectress and later her own mother. Now returned to the family, she is loved by all.
10.modern-da: Elizabeth beskriver hendes historie: optaget i familien Frankenstein, hengiven til fru Frankenstein, plejede hun både sin beskytterinde og senere sin egen mor. Nu vendt tilbage til familien elskes hun af alle.

11.modern-en: Accused of William's murder after the portrait miniature is found in her pocket — planted there by the Creature. Her confused behavior during the night of the murder deepens suspicion.
11.modern-da: Anklaget for Williams mord, efter at portrætminiaturen er fundet i hendes lomme — placeret der af Væsenet. Hendes forvirrede opførsel i mordnatten uddyber mistanken.

12.modern-en: Tried and condemned despite Elizabeth's impassioned defense. Confesses under her confessor's relentless pressure but recants to Elizabeth in prison, declaring her innocence. Executed the next day. Victor is consumed by guilt.
12.modern-da: Stilles for retten og dømmes trods Elizabeths lidenskabelige forsvar. Tilstår under sin skriftefaders ubarmhjertige pres, men tilbagekalder over for Elizabeth i fængslet og erklærer sin uskyld. Henrettes næste dag. Victor fortæres af skyld.

epithet.en: Blind patriarch of the exiled cottage family
epithet.da: Blind patriark for den landsforviste hyttefamilie

15.modern-en: Observed by the Creature: a blind old man who plays the guitar and lives with his children Felix and Agatha in a poor cottage. His gentle nature and the family's mutual devotion captivate the Creature.
15.modern-da: Observeret af Væsenet: en blind gammel mand, der spiller guitar og bor med sine børn Felix og Agatha i en fattig hytte. Hans milde natur og familiens gensidige hengivenhed fængsler Væsenet.

16.modern-en: Continues to be observed through winter. His kindness and the family's love become the Creature's model of human goodness and his deepest longing.
16.modern-da: Fortsætter med at blive observeret gennem vinteren. Hans venlighed og familiens kærlighed bliver Væsenets forbillede for menneskelighed og hans dybeste længsel.

17.modern-en: Welcomes Safie with warmth when she arrives at the cottage. Felix uses books to teach Safie the language, and the Creature learns alongside her.
17.modern-da: Byder Safie varmt velkommen, da hun ankommer til hytten. Felix bruger bøger til at lære Safie sproget, og Væsenet lærer med.

19.modern-en: The Creature enters the cottage when De Lacey is alone. The blind man is sympathetic and kind, offering encouragement. But Felix returns, sees the Creature, and beats him. De Lacey is powerless to intervene.
19.modern-da: Væsenet træder ind i hytten, mens De Lacey er alene. Den blinde mand er forstående og venlig og opmuntrer ham. Men Felix vender tilbage, ser Væsenet og slår ham. De Lacey er magtesløs.

20.modern-en: The family has fled the cottage in terror after Felix's violent encounter with the Creature. They never return, and the Creature is left utterly alone.
20.modern-da: Familien er flygtet fra hytten i rædsel efter Felix' voldelige møde med Væsenet. De vender aldrig tilbage, og Væsenet er efterladt fuldstændigt alene.

epithet.en: De Lacey's son, Safie's devoted lover
epithet.da: De Laceys søn, Safies hengivne elsker

15.modern-en: Observed by the Creature: hardworking and melancholy, he cares for his father and sister in their poverty. His sadness lifts only when doing kindness for others.
15.modern-da: Observeret af Væsenet: hårdtarbejdende og melankolsk tager han sig af sin far og søster i deres fattigdom. Hans tristhed letter kun, når han viser andre godhed.

17.modern-en: Overjoyed by Safie's arrival. Teaches her his language using Volney's Ruins of Empires, which the Creature secretly studies alongside them.
17.modern-da: Overlykkelig over Safies ankomst. Lærer hende sit sprog via Volneys Ruins of Empires, som Væsenet hemmeligt studerer sammen med dem.

18.modern-en: His backstory is revealed: he rescued Safie's Turkish father from unjust execution in Paris, which led to the family's ruin, imprisonment, and exile. The Turkish merchant later betrayed him.
18.modern-da: Hans baggrundshistorie afsløres: han reddede Safies tyrkiske far fra uretfærdig henrettelse i Paris, hvilket førte til familiens ruin, fængsling og eksil. Den tyrkiske købmand forrådte ham senere.

19.modern-en: Returns to the cottage during the Creature's conversation with De Lacey. Horrified at the Creature's appearance, he tears him from his father and beats him with a stick. The Creature flees without retaliating.
19.modern-da: Vender tilbage til hytten under Væsenets samtale med De Lacey. Forfærdet over Væsenets udseende river han ham fra sin far og slår ham med en stok. Væsenet flygter uden at gøre modstand.

20.modern-en: Arranges to leave the cottage permanently, telling the landlord his father's life is in danger. The Creature watches from hiding as the family departs forever.
20.modern-da: Arrangerer at forlade hytten permanent og fortæller udlejeren, at hans fars liv er i fare. Væsenet ser på fra sit skjulested, mens familien rejser for evigt.

17.modern-en: Arrives at the cottage on horseback, a beautiful young woman from Constantinople. Her reunion with Felix transforms the household's mood from melancholy to joy. The Creature learns language alongside her.
17.modern-da: Ankommer til hytten til hest, en smuk ung kvinde fra Konstantinopel. Hendes genforening med Felix forvandler husholdningens stemning fra melankoli til glæde. Væsenet lærer sprog sammen med hende.

18.modern-en: Her backstory: daughter of a Turkish merchant and a Christian Arab mother. Her mother instilled in her a love of independence. After her father's betrayal of Felix, she defied his orders and traveled alone to find her lover in Germany.
18.modern-da: Hendes baggrundshistorie: datter af en tyrkisk købmand og en kristen arabisk mor. Hendes mor indprentede hende en kærlighed til uafhængighed. Efter sin fars forræderi mod Felix trodsede hun hans ordrer og rejste alene for at finde sin elskede i Tyskland.

19.modern-en: Returns to the cottage with Agatha and Felix just as the Creature is speaking to De Lacey. Rushes out of the cottage in terror at the sight of the Creature.
19.modern-da: Vender tilbage til hytten med Agatha og Felix, netop som Væsenet taler med De Lacey. Styrter ud af hytten i rædsel ved synet af Væsenet.

epithet.en: Walton's sister, recipient of the letters

1.modern-en: Addressed as the recipient of Walton's letters. She had worried about the expedition's dangers. Walton writes to reassure her and share his excitement about the voyage north.
1.modern-da: Tiltales som modtager af Waltons breve. Hun havde bekymret sig om ekspeditionens farer. Walton skriver for at berolige hende og dele sin begejstring for rejsen nordpå.

2.modern-en: Walton confides to her his loneliness and desire for a kindred friend. She remains his anchor to home and emotional connection throughout the letters.
2.modern-da: Walton betror hende sin ensomhed og sit ønske om en beslægtet sjæl. Hun forbliver hans anker til hjemmet og følelsesmæssige forbindelse gennem brevene.

28.modern-en: Walton's final letters to Margaret describe Victor's death, the crew's mutiny, the decision to turn south, and the Creature's appearance and farewell. She is the silent audience for the entire tale.
28.modern-da: Waltons sidste breve til Margaret beskriver Victors død, besætningens mytteri, beslutningen om at vende sydpå og Væsenets fremtræden og afsked. Hun er den tavse tilhører til hele fortællingen.
